article_title: Curricular uptake of virtual gaming simulation in nursing education.
citation: Verkuyl M., Lapum J.L., St-Amant O., Hughes M., Romaniuk D. (2021). Curricular uptake of virtual gaming simulation in nursing education. Nurse Education in Practice. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.nepr.2021.102967
title: Virtual gaming simulation (VGS): high-fidelity 2D immersive branching-scenario games for nursing clinical decision-making
description: VGS integrate gaming theory with computerized simulations re-enacting clinical scenarios. The article's games are described as "a high fidelity, 2D immersive simulation using videos of simulated patients (played by actors)" in which users make clinical decisions. A branching scenario approach presents film clips of nurse-client scenarios with options; incorrect choices show consequences and feedback before redirection, and users receive a summary report and can replay. Games cover pediatrics, mental health, maternal health, and emergency, are freely accessible, take up to an hour to play, and have been played over 600,000 times across 25 counties.
requirements: Alignment of VGS learning outcomes with course learning outcomes, standards of practice, and entry-to-practice competencies
Faculty and technological support available so glitches do not overshadow the experience
constraints: High quality VGS are expensive to produce, though unlimited reuse mitigates some costs
Open access with no log in means the team does not know players' disciplines, year of nursing, or demographics
examples: The games are freely accessible at de.ryerson.ca/games/nursing/hospital and have been integrated into curricula at the authors' institutions, internationally, and for continuing competence
key_sources: Verkuyl M., Lapum J.L., St-Amant O., Hughes M., Romaniuk D. (2021). Curricular uptake of virtual gaming simulation in nursing education. Nurse Education in Practice. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.nepr.2021.102967

article_title: Virtual Global Collaboration in Data Analytics and Machine Learning Education: A Mixed-Methods Study of Asynchronous Cross-Border Teamwork
citation: Sehrish Basir Nizamani, Saad Nizamani, Khyati Goyal, Sarwat Nizamani, Zannah Ziew. (2026). Virtual Global Collaboration in Data Analytics and Machine Learning Education: A Mixed-Methods Study of Asynchronous Cross-Border Teamwork. Accepted to the 2026 IEEE Frontiers in Education Conference (FIE). https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01147
title: Conceptual framework of VGC outcomes: three mediating dimensions (collaborative experience, communication and cultural dynamics, logistical strategies) influence three outcome dimensions
description: The article proposes a conceptual framework in which VGC participation influences student outcomes through "three interconnected mediating dimensions: collaborative experience, communication and cultural dynamics, and logistical strategies." These mediators are expected to influence three primary outcome dimensions: learning and skill development, perceived value, and global citizenship and readiness, plus challenges and opportunities as a reflective outcome. The framework is informed by research on collaborative learning, computer-supported collaborative learning, and virtual exchange, and generated hypotheses H1-H7 tested in the study.
requirements: Requires course-embedded VGC participation in mixed-institution teams on shared disciplinary tasks as the instructional context
constraints: The framework assumes outcomes depend on quality of interaction, communication, and coordination, not only the task itself
target_learning_goals: technical data analytics and machine learning skills
examples: The framework's seven constructs were operationalized in a post-project survey with five-point Likert items, and all seven hypotheses were supported.
